takeaway: Nitric oxide (NO) is a cell-signalling molecule: made on demand, diffuses out of nerve terminals (not in vesicles) and is released by endothelium as endothelium-derived relaxing factor.

question.text: Which one of the following molecules is used for cell signalling?
question.say: Which one of the following molecules is used for cell signalling?

lines.text: Nitric oxide is a gas messenger. At the nerve terminal it is made instantly, as needed.
It is not packed in vesicles. It simply diffuses out of the terminal over a few seconds.
Blood vessel endothelium also releases it, as endothelium-derived relaxing factor, loosening the muscle wall like an unbuckled belt.
It diffuses into the nearby nerve, especially in brain areas for long-term behaviour and memory.
Carbon dioxide, oxygen, nitrogen and carbonic acid are not used this way, so they are crossed out.
The signalling molecule is nitric oxide.
